title: Query-path telemetry heatmap and SLO decomposition for analytics ingestion
creator: Amina Zhou
description: Add end-to-end telemetry and visualization for the query (read) path of the analytics pipeline focusing on cold-path vs hot-path behavior, cost attribution, and SLO decomposition. This ticket covers SLI definitions, trace instrumentation additions, heatmap dashboards for tail latency drivers, per-tenant high-cardinality sampling strategy, and automated synthetic probes that exercise cold-path flows. Goal is to make it possible to answer: (1) why did this query miss cache / go to cold path, (2) which stage (ingest/router/batcher/runtime/model) contributed most to observed tail latency, and (3) how much did this query cost in tokens / compute units so we can tie cost to SLO burn rate.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document query-level SLIs: p50/p95/p99 total latency, model-inference latency, queueing time, router lookup time, KV cache hit rate
Implement distributed trace spans for router, batcher, runtime dispatch, and model invocation with consistent trace IDs propagated through the pipeline
Create Grafana heatmap dashboards that decompose tail latency by stage and show cold-path frequency across tenants
Per-tenant cost attribution available in dashboard via ingest-ids and token/compute metrics for sampled queries
Adaptive sampling configured for high-cardinality tenants with documented sampling rules and expected coverage
Synthetic cold-path probes running from the synthetic orchestrator that alert when cold-path p95 exceeds threshold
Alerting rules created for SLO burn-rate and correlated with cost-per-query anomalies

risks_and_mitigations: High-cardinality tenant labels could blow up metrics storage -> mitigation: use label shredding + adaptive sampling and only surface full-tenant breakdowns in logs linked from dashboards
Instrumentation CPU overhead may increase latency -> mitigation: emit spans asynchronously, add rate-limits per host, and measure CPU delta in canary before full rollout
Sampling bias missing rare cold-path events -> mitigation: synthetic cold-path probes and anomaly-triggered boosted sampling
Cost attribution errors due to model price volatility -> mitigation: snapshot effective GPU rates hourly and include versioned price source in dashboards
